A Pool resource groups volumes with the same rules: how long their data is kept, how big they get, how they are labeled and recycled.

## Examples

**Full backups kept for a year on disk**

```text
Pool {
  Name = Full
  Pool Type = Backup
  Recycle = yes
  Auto Prune = yes
  Volume Retention = 365 days
  Maximum Volume Bytes = 50G
  Maximum Volumes = 100
  Label Format = "Full-"
  Action On Purge = Truncate
}
```

**Incrementals: one volume per job**

```text
Pool {
  Name = Incremental
  Pool Type = Backup
  Volume Retention = 30 days
  Maximum Volume Jobs = 1
  Label Format = "Incremental-"
}
```

With one job per volume a volume can be recycled as soon as its single job has expired.

### Name {#d-name}

Key: `name` · Type: name · Required

Name of the pool.

```text
Pool {
  Name = "Full"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add pool name=Full
```

### Description {#d-description}

Key: `description` · Type: string

Free text describing the pool.

```text
Pool {
  Name = Full
  Description = "Full backups, kept one year"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add pool name=Full description="Full backups, kept one year"
```

### Pool Type {#d-pooltype}

Key: `pooltype` · Type: enum · Default: `Backup` · Values: `Backup`, `Copy`, `Cloned`, `Archive`, `Migration`, `Scratch`

Kind of pool: Backup (the normal case), Copy, Cloned, Archive, Migration or Scratch. Only Backup pools are used for backups; a pool named Scratch serves as the default scratch pool.

```text
Pool {
  Name = Full
  Pool Type = Backup
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add pool name=Full pooltype=Backup
```

### Label Format {#d-labelformat}

Key: `labelformat` · Type: string

Template for the names of volumes the Director labels automatically. Without it, volumes must be labeled by hand (label). The Director appends a 4-digit number unless the format uses variables such as ${NumVols}. For disk storage the Storage Daemon's device also needs Label Media = yes.

```text
Pool {
  Name = Full
  Label Format = "Full-"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add pool name=Full labelformat=Full-
```

### Label Type {#d-labeltype}

Key: `labeltype` · Type: enum · Deprecated

Deprecated: ANSI or IBM tape labels.

```text
Pool {
  Name = Full
  Label Type = Bareos
}
```

### Cleaning Prefix {#d-cleaningprefix}

Key: `cleaningprefix` · Type: string · Default: `CLN`

Volumes whose name starts with this prefix are cleaning tapes and are never used for data.

```text
Pool {
  Name = Full
  Cleaning Prefix = "CLN"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add pool name=Full cleaningprefix=CLN
```

### Use Catalog {#d-usecatalog}

Key: `usecatalog` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Keep the volumes of this pool in the catalog; should stay yes.

```text
Pool {
  Name = Full
  Use Catalog = yes
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add pool name=Full usecatalog=yes
```

### Purge Oldest Volume {#d-purgeoldestvolume}

Key: `purgeoldestvolume` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

When the pool needs a volume and none is free, purge the oldest volume regardless of its retention. Dangerous: data that should still be kept is lost.

```text
Pool {
  Name = Full
  Purge Oldest Volume = no
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add pool name=Full purgeoldestvolume=no
```

### Action On Purge {#d-actiononpurge}

Key: `actiononpurge` · Type: enum · Values: `None`, `Truncate`

What happens to a volume when it is purged: Truncate shrinks a disk volume to zero to free the space (done by truncate or purge ... action=truncate); None keeps it.

```text
Pool {
  Name = Full
  Action On Purge = Truncate
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add pool name=Full actiononpurge=Truncate
```

Key: `recycleoldestvolume` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

When a volume is needed, prune the oldest volume and reuse it if its retention allows.

```text
Pool {
  Name = Full
  Recycle Oldest Volume = no
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add pool name=Full recycleoldestvolume=no
```

Key: `recyclecurrentvolume` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

When a volume is needed, prune the current volume and reuse it if its retention allows.

```text

  Name = Full
  Recycle Current Volume = no
```

### Maximum Volumes {#d-maximumvolumes}

Key: `maximumvolumes` · Type: positive integer

Upper limit of volumes in the pool; automatic labeling stops there. Together with Maximum Volume Bytes it caps the disk space of the pool.

```text
Pool {
  Name = Full
  Maximum Volumes = 30
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add pool name=Full maximumvolumes=30
```

### Maximum Volume Jobs {#d-maximumvolumejobs}

Key: `maximumvolumejobs` · Type: positive integer

Number of jobs after which a volume is marked Used. With 1, each job gets its own volume, which makes recycling of disk volumes precise.

```text
Pool {
  Name = Full
  Maximum Volume Jobs = 1
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add pool name=Full maximumvolumejobs=1
```

### Maximum Volume Files {#d-maximumvolumefiles}

Key: `maximumvolumefiles` · Type: positive integer

Number of files after which a volume is marked Used.

```text
Pool {
  Name = Full
  Maximum Volume Files = 100000
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add pool name=Full maximumvolumefiles=100000
```

### Maximum Volume Bytes {#d-maximumvolumebytes}

Key: `maximumvolumebytes` · Type: size

Size after which a volume is marked Full. On disk storage this keeps volumes small enough to be recycled one by one. Sizes take the suffixes k, m, g, t (powers of 1024) or kb, mb, gb, tb (powers of 1000).

```text
Pool {
  Name = Full
  Maximum Volume Bytes = 50 g
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add pool name=Full maximumvolumebytes="50 g"
```

### Catalog Files {#d-catalogfiles}

Key: `catalogfiles` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Store the file records of the jobs in this pool. Without them no single files can be selected for restore, only whole jobs.

```text
Pool {
  Name = Full
  Catalog Files = yes
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add pool name=Full catalogfiles=yes
```

### Volume Retention {#d-volumeretention}

Key: `volumeretention` · Type: time · Default: `31536000` (1 year)

How long the jobs on a volume are kept after the volume was last written. When it has run out, the jobs and files on it can be pruned and the volume recycled. It is the main retention setting in Bareos 25. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

```text
Pool {
  Name = Full
  Volume Retention = 1 year
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add pool name=Full volumeretention="1 year"
```

### Volume Use Duration {#d-volumeuseduration}

Key: `volumeuseduration` · Type: time

How long a volume is written to after its first write; then it is marked Used. Without it, a volume stays Append until it is full. Useful to get one volume per day or week. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

```text
Pool {
  Name = Full
  Volume Use Duration = 23 hours
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add pool name=Full volumeuseduration="23 hours"
```

### Migration Time {#d-migrationtime}

Key: `migrationtime` · Type: time

For Migrate jobs with Selection Type PoolTime: jobs older than this are migrated. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

```text
Pool {
  Name = Full
  Migration Time = 30 days
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add pool name=Full migrationtime="30 days"
```

Key: `migrationhighbytes` · Type: size

For Selection Type PoolOccupancy: migration starts when the pool holds more than this. Sizes take the suffixes k, m, g, t (powers of 1024) or kb, mb, gb, tb (powers of 1000).

```text

  Name = Full
  Migration High Bytes = 800 g
}
```

In the console:

### Migration Low Bytes {#d-migrationlowbytes}

Key: `migrationlowbytes` · Type: size

For Selection Type PoolOccupancy: migration stops when the pool is below this. Sizes take the suffixes k, m, g, t (powers of 1024) or kb, mb, gb, tb (powers of 1000).

```text

  Name = Full
  Migration Low Bytes = 600 g
}
```

In the console:

Key: `autoprune` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no`

### Recycle {#d-recycle}

Key: `recycle` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Allow volumes of this pool to be reused once they are purged. With no, a full volume keeps its data until it is relabeled or deleted.

```text

  Name = Full
  Recycle = yes
}
```

In the console:

```text

```

Key: `recyclepool` · Type: resource

### Minimum Block Size {#d-minimumblocksize}

Key: `minimumblocksize` · Type: size

Minimum block size for volumes of this pool, for tape drives with special needs. Sizes take the suffixes k, m, g, t (powers of 1024) or kb, mb, gb, tb (powers of 1000).

```text
Pool {
  Name = Full
  Minimum Block Size = 64 k

```

In the console:

### Maximum Block Size {#d-maximumblocksize}

Key: `maximumblocksize` · Type: size

Maximum block size for volumes of this pool; larger blocks speed up modern tape drives. Volumes written with one size must be read with it. Sizes take the suffixes k, m, g, t (powers of 1024) or kb, mb, gb, tb (powers of 1000).

```text
Pool {
  Name = Full
  Maximum Block Size = 1 m
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add pool name=Full maximumblocksize="1 m"
```
